blogs.title: Breaking the Transformer Bottleneck: Why LSTMs Are Coming Back (Coins The Best)
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the paper's central thesis: while Transformers ruled the scene for years, LSTMs are being revScaled to billions of parameters to compete again. This post explains why, and introduces xLSTM as the new contender built on old-school gating mechanics.

blogs.title: The Memory Matrix Mystery: How xLSTM Stores More Than Just Numbers
blogs.description: A deep dive into the revolutionary part of the paper: replacing single memory numbers (scalars) with memory matrices. We use analogies of 'digital sticky notes' and 'insurance claims' to explain how this matrix update rule solves problems that older models struggle with, effectively doubling the storage density.

blogs.title: State Tracking for the Ages: Solving Real-World Problems with Memory Mixing
blogs.description: Exploring the 'state tracking' capabilities enabled by xLSTM's exponential gates. Through examples like tracking entities in long stories or spotting patterns in code, this post shows how xLSTM's unique ability to revise storage decisions makes it superior for complex engineering and creative tasks compared to static attention models.

blogs.title: Linear Scaling vs Quadratic Chaos: The Speed Advantage of xLSTM
blogs.description: A technical yet simplified look at the computational complexities. Learn why xLSTM is linear in context length (meaning it handles 100x longer text just as fast as 10x) compared to Transformers, which become exponentially slower as data grows. Plus, a breakdown of how its parallel processing architecture beats state-of-the-art models.
